messages:
Anya Kapoor: Quick legal check — we're finishing Prophetix-2.7B onboarding. License text says 'no redistribution of weights' but allows 'internal hosting for evaluation'. We're planning: host quantized int8 weights behind Dedicated/Private and also ship a quant bundle to a handful of enterprise customers that requested on-prem copies. Is that a redistribution violation? Also seeing small eval regressions after quant, want to confirm whether any quality caveats change licensing obligations.
Mohit Rao: Short answer: depends on how the license defines 'redistribute'. If 'redistribute' includes providing binary weight files to third parties, shipping on-prem copies is probably not allowed. Hosting behind our service should be fine if the license permits internal hosting.
Liam Chen: FWIW our int8 run of Prophetix-2.7B: MMLU drop ~0.8pt, Rouge-L on summarization -1.2, latency down 3.6x. Regression is small but noticeable on some prompts. We added a quantized-readme with eval caveats.
Zoe Martinez: Product note — several pilot customers explicitly asked for a local bundle (airgapped). They said they'd pay for an on-prem license. If legal disallows redistribution we need to communicate no-download constraint up front.
Evelyn (Legal): Copying the relevant clause we reviewed. Excerpt: ```Section 4(b) Redistribution: "Licensee shall not redistribute, sublicense, or publish Model Weight files in binary or source form to third parties without express written permission from Licensor."``` Based on that language, handing over weight files to customers is redistribution. Hosting within a managed service (Dedicated or Private) where we keep custody is generally permitted under 'internal hosting' wording, but sending copies = redistribution.
Evelyn (Legal): Also a provenance/exportability note: some upstream models include an attribution plus export-control paragraph. We need to check export-control flags for Prophetix — I flagged the repo for export review.
Mohit Rao: Operationally, hosting-only is easy: keep weights in our internal bucket, restrict downloads, enable KMS/HSM, and add telemetry. Shipping on-prem bundles would require a separate outbound-license from upstream.
Liam Chen: For the quant/regression side: if we can't ship a bundle, customers requesting airgapped runs could use Redwood Private (we'll deploy inside their VPC) with the same model. Performance/accuracy tradeoffs documented.
Zoe Martinez: Can Legal draft the exact customer-facing language? Something like: "Prophetix-2.7B (quantized) is available for hosting via Redwood Dedicated/Private. Upstream license prohibits distribution of weight files; we cannot provide weight binaries for download."
Evelyn (Legal): Yep. Draft: "Prophetix-2.7B is provided under upstream license which prohibits redistribution of model weights. Redwood may host the model on your behalf (Dedicated or Private deployments) but cannot provide downloadable weight files without separate permission from the model licensor. Customer is responsible for verifying export-control requirements for their geography." Feel free to shorten.
model-bot: Model Prophetix-2.7B uploaded to onboarding queue. Onboarding status: license-check pending export-review.
Anya Kapoor: Thanks — that's what I expected. Next steps: 1) Mohit/Eng infra: add bucket/download restriction, KMS requirement, and docs link to quant-eval caveats; 2) Legal/Evelyn: get a short customer-facing blurb and confirm export flags; 3) Product/Zoe: tell pilots the hosting-only constraint and offer Redwood Private as alternative. I'll update the onboarding checklist and add a link to the quantized benchmark table. :thumbsup:
Mohit Rao: I'll open an infra ticket and tag @security for KMS/HSM requirements.
Liam Chen: I'll add the detailed eval table to the model card and mark the quant run as 'experimental' until we finish a few more prompts.
Evelyn (Legal): I'll ping upstream for redistribution permission, but don't promise a yes. If they decline, we proceed hosting-only and mark the onboarding record with 'no-export'.
Zoe Martinez: Sending updated messaging to pilots now.
Anya Kapoor: Great. Closing the thread once infra ticket exists.
